items.title: Africa Via, AXIAN, PIDG and FMO Sign EUR 50 Million Financing Agreement for the Kong Solaire Project
items.summary: Kong Solaire SAS, a project company owned by Africa Via, Axian and the Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG) through InfraCo, its project development solution, has signed a financing agreement with FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, for the Kong solar photovoltaic power plant in Côte d’Ivoire. FMO is providing the project’s entire long-term financing, amounting to up to EUR 55.5 million, with a 20-year tenor. items.title: Kong Solaire signs 20-year FMO financing for 50MWp of solar in northern Côte d’Ivoire
items.summary: FMO is providing all the long-term debt for Kong Solaire, a 50MWp plant near Kong in northern Côte d’Ivoire developed by Africa Via, in which AXIAN holds a majority, and PIDG’s InfraCo. Construction is under way, with commissioning planned for 2028 and power sold to CI-ENERGIES for 25 years. Work on Kong Solaire began with the Ivorian State in 2020, according to Minkaila Salami, chief executive of the developer Africa Via.

items.title: Oyo gets 17.7MW of interconnected mini-grids as Tegbe rules out a tariff rise
items.summary: Minister of Power Joseph Tegbe has flagged off five interconnected hybrid solar mini-grids totalling 17.7MW across five local government areas of Oyo State. They are financed by the World Bank and developed by Paras Energy, and Tegbe told Nigerians there is no plan to raise electricity tariffs. Five interconnected hybrid solar mini-grids with a combined 17.7MW are going up across Oyo State, at Bola, Jiboye, Molade-Adelubi, Ogo Oluwa and Sooko-Elega. Minister of Power Joseph Tegbe flagged off construction in Ibadan on 16 October on behalf of President Bola Tinubu.
